requirement: Build a fake callable that fails and succeeds in a scripted order, and a retry helper that retries only chosen exceptions for a bounded number of attempts, re-raising the last failure.
skeleton: flaky creating a Mock with a list side_effect after an empty check, and a generic call_with_retry validating attempts, looping attempts minus one times with a filtered except, then making the final call outside the loop.
caption: Retry logic tested against a scripted fake built with unittest.mock. flaky(*outcomes) raises ValueError saying flaky needs at least one outcome when called with nothing, and otherwise returns a Mock whose side_effect is a list of the outcomes: each call consumes the next one, raising it when it is an exception instance and returning it otherwise, and a call after the list is exhausted raises StopIteration. The mock also records call_count for assertions. call_with_retry(func, attempts=3, retry_on=(ConnectionError,)) raises ValueError saying attempts must be at least 1 for a non-positive count. It then calls func inside a loop over range(attempts - 1), returning the first success and continuing only when the raised exception is one of retry_on; any other exception propagates immediately. The final attempt is made outside the loop so its exception, such as the last ConnectionError, reaches the caller unchanged. The fixture asserts that one ConnectionError then ok returns ok after two calls, that three ConnectionErrors re-raise the third after exactly three calls, that a ValueError is raised after one call, that attempts=1 calls once, that TimeoutError can be made retryable, that attempts=0 raises ValueError, and that flaky with no outcomes raises ValueError while an exhausted flaky raises StopIteration.

plan.intent: Test retries against a scripted flaky dependency
constraints: Outcomes are raised or returned one per call, in order
Retries stop after the configured number of attempts
The last failure is re-raised unchanged
flaky with no outcomes raises ValueError

rationale.teaches: Mock(side_effect=[...]) mixing exception instances and return values to script a dependency, with call_count proving how many attempts ran.
rationale.why: Retry code is usually tested only on the happy path, so off-by-one attempt counts and over-broad excepts pass until a real outage.

ops.docstring: Script a flaky dependency with Mock side_effect to exercise retry logic.

candidates.why_wrong: The loop makes one attempt too many before the final call.
Every exception is retried, including errors that can never succeed.
A single side_effect repeats the first outcome forever instead of stepping through them.
attempts=0 still calls the function once instead of raising ValueError.
The default allows only two attempts instead of three.
